note: Use the lemma that every odd-length closed walk contains an odd cycle: choose a shortest odd closed walk; any repeated internal vertex splits it into two shorter closed walks whose lengths sum to an odd number, so one is shorter and odd, contradiction. Hence the shortest walk has no repeated vertex except its equal endpoints and is a cycle. Under the no-odd-cycle hypothesis, all closed walks are therefore even. In each connected component choose a root; all root-to-vertex walks have one parity because concatenating two such walks (one reversed) gives a closed walk. Partition by parity. Appending an edge flips parity, so every edge crosses the partition. The forward implication is alternation of sides around a cycle.
The exact target theorem is now verifier-accepted and present in the fact graph; no predecessor facts were required.
